questions.stem: Which of the following defines the fade margin reported in the Radio Mobile link checks?
questions.key: The signal level in dB above the receiver threshold
distractors: The signal level at the receiver in dBm
The share of the Fresnel zone left clear by terrain
The power lost in the line between radio and antenna
questions.explanation: The study reports every link as a margin above the -119 dBm threshold; for example the weakest link, Daraga to Relay Alpha, holds +35.8 dB.
why: That is the RX level, a separate figure on the same link slide.
That is the Fresnel figure, also reported separately.
That is the line loss, recorded at 0.5 dB, not a margin.

questions.stem: Which combination matches the Radio Mobile settings recorded for the study?
questions.key: Longley-Rice (ITM) on SRTM-3 90 m terrain data with a 10 km plot radius
distractors: Egli on SRTM-3 90 m terrain data with a 10 km plot radius
Longley-Rice (ITM) on SRTM-3 90 m terrain data with a 30 km plot radius
Longley-Rice (ITM) on 30 m terrain data with a 10 km plot radius
questions.explanation: Slide 15 records the Longley-Rice model (ITM, k = 4/3), SRTM-3 90 m DEM terrain data and a 10 km plot radius per station.
why: Egli is the model used for the cellular CloudRF plots, not the Radio Mobile plots.
The recorded plot radius is 10 km per station, not 30 km.
The recorded terrain data is the SRTM-3 90 m DEM, not 30 m data.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Relay Alpha?
questions.key: A 10 W retransmission site on Pocdol high ground, 931 m above sea level with a 6 m mast
distractors: A 5 W base station on the lower Mayon slopes with a 30 m mast
A 10 W HF NVIS station beside Brigade HQ in Legazpi City
A cellular tower on the coastal highway modelled in CloudRF
questions.explanation: Relay Alpha is emplaced at 51P XQ 01711 40097 on Pocdol high ground, 931 m ground elevation with a 6 m mast, as a 10 W retransmission site.
why: Mayon's 6 km Permanent Danger Zone allows no relay sites, and Relay Alpha is not a 5 W base.
HF NVIS is the alternate means in PACE, not the relay.
CloudRF was used for cellular towers, not for the VHF relay.

questions.stem: Which combination matches the CloudRF inputs recorded for the cellular exports?
questions.key: Egli, 780 MHz, 20 W with 12 dBi at 30 m, handset at 1.5 m
distractors: Longley-Rice, 780 MHz, 20 W with 12 dBi at 30 m, handset at 1.5 m
Egli, 40-59 MHz, 5 W with 4 dBi at 6 m, handset at 2 m
Egli, 780 MHz, 10 W with 4 dBi at 6 m, handset at 1.5 m
questions.explanation: Slides 37-38 record Egli at 780 MHz, 20 W, a 12 dBi transmit antenna at 30 m AGL and a 1.5 m receive height for the cellular exports.
why: Longley-Rice is the Radio Mobile model; the cellular exports use Egli.
40-59 MHz, 5 W, 4 dBi at 6 m and a 2 m handset are the Radio Mobile handheld-net settings, not the cellular inputs.
The cellular transmit power is 20 W with 12 dBi at 30 m; 10 W and 4 dBi at 6 m are the relay and HQ settings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is supported about the cellular comparison on a common map extent?
questions.key: The same extent supports comparison but does not establish complete service coverage
distractors: The 51% corridor figure proves complete coverage by all three networks
The 12 key towers represent every CellMapper tower in the AO
The model inputs describe the operators' verified equipment and service
questions.explanation: The slide says the common map extent supports comparison and does not establish complete service coverage, and that the inputs describe the exports, not verified equipment.
why: Only 51% of the corridor is covered by the 12 modelled towers.
The other CellMapper towers were not run because of the credit cap.
Slide 38 says the model inputs describe the exports, not the operators' equipment.

questions.stem: It is corridor land with no plotted signal or only the weakest Radio Mobile classes, shown as red hatch.
distractors: A Fresnel zone
A radio basin
A plot radius
questions.explanation: The study maps three dead spots; DS-1 is 179 km2 across the Daraga-Castilla seam.
why: The Fresnel zone describes clearance around the direct path.
A radio basin is a connected area of coverage; the study joins two basins into one brigade net.
The plot radius is the 10 km extent computed per station.

questions.stem: It is the setting recorded as -119 dBm (0.25 microvolt sensitivity) in the Radio Mobile setup.
distractors: Transmit power
Line loss
Fade margin
questions.explanation: The setup slide lists the RX threshold as -119 dBm; link margins are measured above it.
why: Transmit power was 5 W for stations and 10 W for the relay.
Line loss was recorded as 0.5 dB.
Fade margin is computed above the threshold, not set as a threshold.

questions.stem: A planner raises the HQ mast from 2 m to 30 m and sees the margin move only from 35.2 to 35.9 dB. What does the study conclude about mast height at 40-59 MHz?
questions.key: Mast height barely matters at these frequencies
distractors: Mast height is the main way to cross the Pocdol range
Every base station should be raised to the maximum mast height
Taller masts are needed for the Daraga link to close
questions.explanation: The study states that mast height barely matters at 40-59 MHz and that height does not cross the Pocdol range; the relay does.
why: The recommendation says height does not cross the Pocdol range; the relay does.
At 6 m the links already close, so maximum masts are not needed.
Every one of the 12 links already closes at planned heights.

questions.stem: After Relay Alpha is added, the 179 km2 DS-1 dead spot shrinks to about what area?
distractors: 6 km2
14 km2
81 km2
questions.explanation: The before-and-after slide shows DS-1 falling from 179 km2 to 15 km2, with corridor coverage rising from 81% to 96%.
why: 6 km2 is the area of DS-2 at Sto. Domingo.
14 km2 is the area of DS-3 at Oas / Ligao.
81 is the before-relay corridor percentage, not an area.

questions.stem: A signal officer reads the scorecard of the 12 planned links for the one with the least room for worsening conditions. Which link is it?
questions.key: Daraga to Relay Alpha, 28.4 km at +35.8 dB
distractors: Legazpi City TOC to Relay Alpha, 27.1 km at +57.2 dB
Relay Alpha to Casiguran, 18.6 km at +67.0 dB
Sorsogon City to Bacon District, 5.1 km at +54.8 dB
questions.explanation: The Daraga to Relay Alpha link has the smallest fade margin, +35.8 dB, though it still closes.
why: That link is longer than most but holds +57.2 dB.
That link holds +67.0 dB, well above the weakest.
That link holds +54.8 dB, well above the weakest.

questions.stem: Handhelds are used inside buildings in Legazpi City and Sorsogon City, the densest LGUs. What does the study advise?
questions.key: Expect a 10-20 dB loss and use vehicle or base sets for C2 there
distractors: Raise handheld masts to 30 m to recover the loss
Move classified traffic to cellular in the towns
Rely on Relay Alpha's 10 W retransmission alone for building coverage
questions.explanation: The planning factors say handhelds lose 10-20 dB inside buildings, so vehicle or base sets should be used for C2 in dense urban clutter.
why: Mast height barely matters at these frequencies, and handhelds do not use 30 m masts.
Cellular is a contingency means only and never for classified traffic.
The relay serves the Daraga-Castilla gap, not in-building loss.

questions.stem: Which list gives the PACE plan of the study's communications architecture in order?
questions.key: VHF FM net via Relay Alpha; HF NVIS; cellular with encrypted apps; SATCOM terminal or runner
distractors: VHF FM net via Relay Alpha; cellular with encrypted apps; HF NVIS; SATCOM terminal or runner
HF NVIS; VHF FM net via Relay Alpha; cellular with encrypted apps; SATCOM terminal or runner
VHF FM net via Relay Alpha; HF NVIS; SATCOM terminal or runner; cellular with encrypted apps
questions.explanation: Primary is the VHF FM net via Relay Alpha, Alternate HF NVIS, Contingency cellular with encrypted apps, and Emergency a SATCOM terminal or runner.
why: Cellular is the contingency, so it follows HF NVIS.
The relay net is the primary, ahead of HF NVIS.
SATCOM or runner is the emergency, last in the plan.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three dead spots mapped in the study?
distractors: The Daraga-Castilla seam on the Manito slopes
Sto. Domingo / Mayon SE
Oas / Ligao NW ridge
questions.explanation: The study maps DS-1 at the Daraga-Castilla seam, DS-2 at Sto. Domingo / Mayon SE and DS-3 at Oas / Ligao NW. Bacon District is a Sorsogon unit reached by Relay Alpha.
why: That is DS-1, the largest dead spot.
That is DS-2.
That is DS-3.
